name: Orkney (Mainland Orkney ORS)
tests_run: Petrography/mineralogy + pXRF of field samples of the main ORS units (Bevins et al. 2024, reviewed); heavy minerals - chrome spinel:zircon index CZi, mean 1.3 from 35 Lower/Middle/Upper ORS samples; detrital zircon compilation (Sassnowski 2015, Fig. 12d, Caithness + Orkney Middle/Upper ORS); clay I/S expandability (Hillier & Clayton 1989)
paper_conclusion: Excluded. Bevins et al. (2024) 'interpreted that the Altar Stone could not have been derived from Orkney'; I/S expandability <10 in Caithness and Orkney vs c. 20% in the Altar Stone 'would exclude Caithness and Orkney'; chrome spinel is very scarce. Zircon spectrum is, however, similar to the Altar Stone's (Fig. 12d).

name: Orcadian Basin - NE Scotland mainland (outcrops labelled 'Orcadian Basin')
formation_or_basin: Orcadian Basin, ORS (Fig. 11); text names Caithness, Sutherland, Tarbat Peninsula/Inner Moray Firth (see unmapped rows)
tests_run: Whole-basin comparison: chrome spinel/CZi, detrital zircon, clay mineralogy and thermal maturity, Ba stream-sediment geochemistry (Fig. 11)
paper_conclusion: Partly excluded. Abstract: 'many outcrops of the Old Red Sandstone (ORS) in the Orcadian Basin could not have been the source'. Chrome spinel is scarce across the basin; clay data exclude significant areas of Caithness and Sutherland; parts of the Moray Firth are not excluded by clay but are 'discounted based on the heavy mineral data'. Ba anomalies noted to the south of the Inner Moray Firth. Conclusions: no examined outcrop matches.

name: Midland Valley Basin (Scotland)
tests_run: Petrography (Phillips 2007 review); detrital zircon U-Pb (McKellar et al. 2020; Phillips et al. 2009, Fig. 12f-h; none for ORS elsewhere in the Midland Valley); clay I/S expandability (Marshall et al. 1994; Hillier et al. 2006); tosudite occurrence; modern heavy mineral data not available for this basin (text)
paper_conclusion: Contradictory in the paper. Petrography and sedimentology (citing Phillips 2007): abundant lithic grains 'clearly demonstrates that the Altar Stone could not have been derived from the Silurian–Devonian sequences in the Midland Valley Basin of Scotland'; 'the data from Phillips (2007) would also exclude the ORS from the Midland Valley of Scotland'. Other sections leave the basin, or parts of it, open. Heavy mineral suite: 'virtually no modern heavy mineral data available from intervening parts of the ORS basins, from the Scottish Midland Valley to the Anglo-Welsh borderland, which would therefore remain possible source areas from a heavy mineral standpoint'. Detrital ages: only the overlying ORS of the NE Midland Valley (Dunnottar-Crawton, Arbuthnott-Garvock and Strathmore groups) 'can be discounted'; 'There have been no zircon U–Pb studies of the ORS elsewhere in the Midland Valley'. Clay mineralogy: Stonehaven and Arbuthnott groups have too-low I/S expandability; Strathmore Group clay is comparable but discounted on zircon. The Abstract and Conclusions do not name the Midland Valley (Conclusions: other examined areas 'can all so far be excluded when all aspects of the multi-proxy analysis are considered'). Introduction notes prior work placed possible sources in 'the Midland Valley or Orcadian Basin'. Specific NE and southern-margin units are recorded separately (U06–U08) and remain excluded.
